data.description:
## Goal

Execute the 24-hour experiment: apply the STE100 instruction to AGENTS_GLOBAL.md, let it run for 24h, measure metrics, produce comparison report, and revert.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Add the sentence to AGENTS_GLOBAL.md (verified via grep).
2. Record exact wall-clock T0 and commit hash.
3. Run analysis at T0+24h for both [T0-24h, T0) and [T0, T0+24h) windows.
4. Produce comparison report at `docs/experiments/ste100-24h/report.md` with:
   - Metrics table (session count, duration, tokens, cost for both windows)
   - Delta percentages and direction for each metric
   - Notable outliers (output-token-limit errors, extreme sessions)
   - Project and model breakdown
   - One-line interpretation per metric
5. Revert the AGENTS_GLOBAL.md change (verified via grep).
6. Record revert commit hash.

## Steps

1. Start parent implementation
2. Implement child tasks first (analysis script + tests)
3. Add STE100 sentence to AGENTS_GLOBAL.md, commit to dev, record T0
4. Wait 24 hours (or set reminder/automation)
5. Run analysis for baseline window [T0-24h, T0)
6. Run analysis for experiment window [T0, T0+24h)
7. Generate comparison report
8. Revert AGENTS_GLOBAL.md, commit to dev
9. Record results on work item
10. Clean up worktree

## Related

Dependent on: SA-0MU9VSL250092LTY (Build analysis script), SA-0MU9VT5HI001LHKY (Add tests).

data.description:
The end-of-session report helper (`skill/report/scripts/render_report.py`) always renders **Audit: ❔ not run** in the Meta-Data block, even when the work item has a persisted, passing audit.

### Root cause

`wl show <id> --json` returns `auditResult` as a **top-level** key of the response envelope:

```json
{ "success": true, "workItem": { ... }, "auditResult": { "readyToClose": true, ... }, "comments": [...] }
```

`render_metadata()` reads `work_item.get("auditResult")` (line ~235), where `work_item = data.get("workItem", {})` — the top-level `auditResult` is never consulted, so the lookup is always falsy and the audit status degrades to "not run".

Discovered while rendering the final report for SA-0MU7FD0YF0065EG9, whose audit had passed (`readyToClose: true`, all 4 ACs met) yet the report showed "Audit: not run".

### Acceptance Criteria

1. `render_metadata()` resolves audit status from the top-level `auditResult` of the `wl show --json` envelope (falling back to any `workItem.auditResult` for backward compatibility), so a `readyToClose: true` result renders as passed and `readyToClose: false` renders as failed.
2. A unit test covers: top-level `auditResult` with `readyToClose: true` → "passed"; `readyToClose: false` → "failed"; absent/null → "not run".
3. `--json` (stdin) mode continues to work for callers that pass a bare work-item dict.

---

## Filing validation during skill:intake

### Problem statement

Work items are occasionally created or imported into the wrong project's
worklog store (see the 2026-08 pollution incidents in
`docs/dev/worklog-cross-project-protection.md`, where 2,132 foreign `WL-`
items contaminated the SorraAgents store). When `skill:intake` is invoked on
such an item the misfiling silently survives — `wl`'s prefix-to-sibling
resolution even *hides* it by routing commands to another project. Intake
should verify the item's filing location up front, tell the operator when it
is wrong, and offer a safe correction path — so misfiled items are caught at
the earliest workflow stage instead of lingering in the wrong store.

### Users

- **Operators/producers** dispatching `skill:intake` (often via herdr on
  cross-project items) — need a loud, early signal when an item belongs to a
  different project than the one it is filed in, plus a safe offer to recreate
  it there.
- **Implementing agents** resuming intake on an item — must not have work
  silently redirected between stores by prefix resolution when the item is
  misfiled.

Example user stories:

- As an operator, when I invoke `/skill:intake <id>` on an item whose prefix
  is not registered in any sibling project, I want to be told *which* project
  it is filed in/and or belongs to, so I can correct the filing.
- As an operator, when an item references only files of a different project, I
  want a warning and an offer to recreate it under the correct project's
  prefix, so cross-project confusion (SA-0MRCPLA4T002V5TV precedent) stops
  early.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. `skill:intake` runs a filing-location check for the target work item before
   any other mutation, and reports its findings to the operator (stderr
   + work-item comment). The check is **non-blocking**: intake proceeds whether
   or not the item passes the check.
2. The check deterministically classifies the item as one of:
   - **ok** — item prefix matches its resolved store's configured `prefix`;
   - **foreign** — item id prefix differs from its owning store's `prefix:`;
   - **unregistered** — the id prefix matches no sibling project's config;
   - **absent** — the item id is not present in its resolved store;
   - **suspicious** (best-effort) — the description/Key Files reference only
     files of a *different* sibling project's repo (content cross-check).
   Each non-`ok` classification names the likely correct project (from the
   sibling scan) and a suggested target prefix.
3. On a non-`ok` classification the script logs a warning and records an
   idempotent `## Filing location check` comment on the item (re-runs update
   the existing comment, never duplicate). When stdin is an interactive TTY it
   additionally offers (a) continue, or (b) recreate the item in the correct
   project; auto-recreation is only possible via an explicit
   `--misfiled-action recreate` flag and never happens by default.
4. Recreating (when chosen) creates a new item under the target project's
   store/prefix copying title, description, tags, issue type and priority,
   records a `Recreated from <source-id>` reference, and closes the original
   with `--reason "Misfiled: recreated in <target-project> (<target-id>)"`.
   A dry-run `--dry-run` mode prints the would-be recreation without creating.
5. The check lives in a new shared helper `skill/shared/filing_location.py`
   (pure, unit-testable, no side effects) invoked from the intake lifecycle
   script; no other skill changes behaviour in this change.
6. **Tests**: unit tests cover the classification branches (ok / foreign /
   unregistered / absent / suspicious), the idempotent comment update, the
   TTY offer path, and dry-run recreation — plus an e2e test where a
   deliberately misfiled item is detected and recreated.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, `skill/intake/SKILL.md`, and `docs/dev/intake-skill-reference.md`
   (plus any relevant wiki/docs entries).
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

### Constraints

- **Non-blocking and non-destructive by default**: detection may never fail
  intake nor mutate foreign stores; recreation requires the explicit flag.
- **Idempotent**: re-running the check on the same item yields the same
  result and never duplicates comments or recreations.
- **Legitimate cross-project usage stays quiet**: running intake from the
  SorraAgents checkout on a `WL-`/`OSL-` item routed by the prefix-to-sibling
  scan is supported behaviour (`docs/dev/intake-skill-reference.md` § Worklog
  resolution) — that is not a misfiling and must not warn.
- Detection must not depend on the network or the installed `wl` version
  beyond reading `config.yaml` and running `wl show`.
- Respect `.gitignore` when scanning sibling repos.

### Existing state

- No filing validation exists in `skill:intake`; `run_wl` / `resolve_worklog_dir`
  in `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` silently redirect to the sibling store
  matching the id prefix.
- `docs/dev/worklog-cross-project-protection.md` documents `wl doctor
  foreign-items` cleanup (release-side), but nothing catches misfiling at
  intake time.
- Related precedent: SA-0MRCPLA4T002V5TV (type inference/flag correction in
  `/intake`), SA-0MS3CIU0F00066CD (move `/intake` to a skill), SA-0MSC0BM1V0032UYT
  (sync prefix filter).

### Desired change

- New shared helper `skill/shared/filing_location.py` exposing
  `check_filing(item_id, *, cwd, sibling_scan_root=SIBLING_SCAN_ROOT,
  runner=None) -> FilingCheck` (severity ok/foreign/unregistered/absent/
  suspicious + `reasons[]` + `target_project`).
- `skill/intake/scripts/intake.py` gains a `check-filing <id>` subcommand and
  runs it as step 0c right after claim; SKILL.md documents the step.
- Intake CLI gains `--misfiled-action {warn,offer,recreate}` (default
  `warn`), `--recreate-target <project-dir>`, and `--dry-run`.
- `docs/dev/intake-skill-reference.md` and `skill/intake/SKILL.md` describe
  the classification table, the idempotent comment, and the offer/recreate
  flow.

### Key Files

- `skill/shared/filing_location.py` — **new** shared, pure detection helper
  (classification, sibling scan, content cross-check).
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — reuse `resolve_worklog_dir`,
  `_extract_work_item_prefix`, `run_wl` (no changes expected).
- `skill/intake/scripts/intake.py` — `check-filing` subcommand + hookup after
  claim; `--misfiled-action`/`--dry-run` flags; **new file**: `.worklog`-safe
  comment update.
- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` — document step 0c + decision table.
- `docs/dev/intake-skill-reference.md` — maintainer reference section.
- `skill/intake/tests/test_filing_location.py` — **new** unit tests
  (classification, idempotent comment, TTY offer, dry-run).
- `skill/intake/tests/test_intake_fresh_repo_e2e.py` — extend with misfiled-item
  e2e scenario.

### Related work

- **SA-0MRCPLA4T002V5TV** — Implement: Type inference and flag correction in
  `/intake` (completed): intake correctness precedent.
- **SA-0MSC0BM1V0032UYT** — Sync prefix filter (completed): defence-in-depth
  against foreign items in stores.
- **SA-0MRMB6P6M008H4U4** / **SA-0MUKCOW1I001MJ7O** — related skill-script
  robustness fixes (find-related automated report).
- Auto-generated report from `/skill:find-related` (see description section
  delimited by `## Related work (automated report)`).

### Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep**: full project-aware (re)filing of an item into a foreign
  store on *every* skill is out of scope; this change wires intake only, with
  the helper ready for later adoption — do not extend to audit/implement here.
- **False positives in the content cross-check**: the "suspicious" branch is
  best-effort and advisory only — never blocks; tests pin conservative
  thresholds.
- **Recreation duplication risk**: recreation is explicit-flag-only and the
  source item is closed with a reference; a dry-run verifies first.
- **Prefix-scan cost**: the memoized sibling scan already exists; the check
  reuses it and adds a single repository read per suspicious candidate.

### Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (asked 2026-10-16, prior session): "Should this work item stay in
  SorraAgents, or be filed in ContextHub?" — **Answer (Map, research,
  2026-10-27): stays in SorraAgents.** The feature changes the canonical
  `skill:intake` implementation shipped from this repo; the ContextHub `wl`
  CLI is a consumer, not the change target. Prior answer: none recorded.
  Evidence: `skill/intake/scripts/intake.py` and `skill/shared/*` under this
  repo; `.worklog/config.yaml` prefix `SA`.
- Q2 (asked 2026-10-16): "How should 'correct project' be determined?" — **Answer
  (recommended, pending producer confirmation):** use the id prefix vs the
  resolved store's `config.yaml` `prefix:` as the primary deterministic check,
  plus a best-effort content cross-check against sibling repos' file trees
  (AC 2). Source: research of `resolve_worklog_dir` /
  `_find_worklog_dir_by_prefix` in `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`.
- Q3 (asked 2026-10-16): "What should happen on misfiling — (a) warn only,
  (b) warn + offer to recreate, (c) auto-recreate, (d) other?" — **Answer
  (recommended, pending producer confirmation): (b)** warn (non-blocking,
  idempotent comment) + interactive offer on a TTY, with auto-recreate
  explicit-flag-only (`--misfiled-action recreate`); never automatic.
- Q4 (asked 2026-10-16): "Scope: intake only, or all skills?" — **Answer
  (recommended, pending producer confirmation): intake only**, via a shared
  helper other skills may adopt later without behaviour change.

## Problem Statement

Agents repeatedly make the same mistakes when working with pi — using `skill_path` as a bash command instead of the tool, expanding backticks in shell commands, forgetting Python imports, and falling into self-correction loops. A skill that analyses recent session logs to detect these patterns would enable proactive skill improvements and prevent recurring failures.

## Users

- **Agent operator / PI** — receives a structured report of agent confusion patterns and actionable improvement recommendations.
- **Skill authors** — get targeted work items to update SKILL.md files, scripts, or add guardrails.
- **Producers** — understand systemic agent behaviour issues across the project.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Skill reads the last 20 session logs (`.pi/agent/sessions/<project-slug>/*.jsonl`) for the CWD project, sorted by modification time.
2. Heuristic analysis extracts: tool call distribution, thinking-content error signals (keywords: error, fail, retry, incorrect, sorry, wrong, fix, correct, issue, problem, confused, wait, actually, oh, hmm, ah), tool result errors (tracebacks, permission denied, command not found, shell expansion errors), and retry/self-correction patterns.
3. LLM-assisted interpretation (via pi calls) classifies patterns into categories (e.g. "skill invocation confusion", "shell quoting issues", "Python import omissions", "permission issues") and generates recommendations.
4. Structured report rendered in the agent response with: summary of findings, top patterns by frequency, recommended skill improvements, and evidence citations (which sessions showed which patterns).
5. Recommendations are filed as worklog comments on the parent work item.
6. For each actionable recommendation, a child work item is auto-created with issue-type `chore` or `feature`, assigned to Map, and linked via `related-to:<parent-id>` in the description.
7. The skill follows existing project conventions: `skill/agent-log-review/SKILL.md`, `skill/agent-log-review/scripts/`, `skill/agent-log-review/tests/`.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (e.g. `docs/dev/agent-log-review-skill-reference.md`).
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Hybrid approach: heuristics for extraction, LLM for classification — not fully automated LLM-only (too expensive) and not heuristic-only (too noisy).
- Only CWD project sessions; no cross-project analysis.
- Auto-create work items but don't implement them — that's downstream work.
- Must handle v3 session log format (session, model_change, thinking_level_change, message types with content as list of thinking/toolCall parts).

## Existing State

- Session logs exist at `~/.pi/agent/sessions/<project-slug>/*.jsonl` in v3 format.
- Existing skills follow `SKILL.md` + `scripts/` + `tests/` convention.
- Related work: SA-0MSNYWMJJ002CIJ7 (tag pi sessions spawned from skills with `--session-id`), SA-0MSMC8KRS00164VD (24h experiment: measure session length & token use), SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL (RCA and reliability recommendations for audit failures), SA-0MLGZN2IH0HH6JSH (Add 'waiting_for_input' session state).
- Known patterns already visible in current sessions: backtick expansion in bash commands, `skill_path` used as bash command, Python `NameError`/`KeyError` from missing imports, `python` vs `python3`, permission denied on script execution, self-correction loops in thinking content.

## Desired Change

A reusable skill that agents can invoke (e.g. `/skill:agent-log-review`) to periodically analyse session logs, produce reports, and auto-create improvement work items.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/agent-log-review/SKILL.md` — skill definition and invocation docs
- `skill/agent-log-review/scripts/agent_log_review.py` — main analysis script
- `skill/agent-log-review/tests/test_agent_log_review.py` — unit tests
- `docs/dev/agent-log-review-skill-reference.md` — skill reference docs

## Risks & Assumptions

**Assumptions**
- Pi v3 session log format is stable (fields: `session`, `model_change`, `thinking_level_change`, `message` with list content of `thinking`/`toolCall` parts, `toolResult` role).
- `<project-slug>` session directory is derived deterministically from CWD (e.g. `--home-rgardler-projects-SorraAgents--`).
- 20 sessions is a statistically useful sample size for common patterns.

**Risks & mitigations**
- **LLM cost/latency** — 20 logs total several MB; mitigate by sending only distilled heuristic signals (counts, excerpts) to the LLM, not raw logs.
- **False positives** — keyword heuristics over-trigger on legitimate uses of "error" (e.g. error-handling code). Mitigate with context windows and LLM confirmation before filing work items.
- **Huge individual sessions** — streaming line-by-line parse, cap per-session excerpt size.
- **Privacy** — session logs may contain paths/tokens; redact secrets in the report and never persist raw log content outside `.worklog/tmp/`.
- **Scope creep** — do not build auto-fix/auto-edit of skills; keep to report + work-item creation (extra opportunities become linked, not in-scope).

## Related work

- SA-0MSNYWMJJ002CIJ7 — Skills: tag pi sessions spawned from skills with --session-id (helps identify skill-spawned sessions for analysis)
- SA-0MSMC8KRS00164VD — 24h experiment: AGENTS.md STE100 instruction — measure session length & token use vs previous period (analysis pattern)
- SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL — RCA and reliability recommendations: why audit Phase 1/Phase 2 frequently fail (similar RCA approach)
- SA-0MLGZN2IH0HH6JSH — Add 'waiting_for_input' session state (session analysis infrastructure)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Analysis engine — what approach for pattern detection (heuristic only / LLM-assisted / hybrid)?" — Answer (operator): "hybrid". Source: interactive reply. Research: confirmed existing skills use pi calls (e.g. audit Phase 2) so LLM calls from a skill are an established pattern.
- Q: "Scope — which projects' logs, and where should the report go?" — Answer (operator): "the project from which the skill is initiated (CWD), recommendations filed in the worklog, report returned in agent response". Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Recommendations — should the skill auto-create work items, or report-only?" — Answer (operator): "create". Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Permission to create the work item?" — Answer (operator): implied by invoking `/intake` with the seed intent; item SA-0MUEKTJRD0010CGC created. Source: interactive invocation.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MS9AXZ8Q007WKKH** – Fix legacy skill/ path refs introduced by StatusLifecycle migration (500d3f8) (completed)
- **SA-0MPDZDVG00013CQJ** – Implement: Agent push-to-dev behavior (completed)

# tree_coverage truncates wrapped AC bullets

## Discovery

Found while planning SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63: the AC-coverage review reported `coverage_pct: 0.0`
and `recommendation: stop` even though every parent AC is genuinely covered by a child. Root
cause: `extract_acceptance_criteria()` in `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` captures only the first
physical line of each `- ` bullet. Work-item descriptions wrap their AC bullets (as the global
`AGENTS.md`/intake/plan conventions produce), so the parent ACs handed to the Jaccard matcher are
truncated mid-sentence:

```
'**AC1 — Hermetic git usage:** every test helper that runs real `git` commands'
```

instead of the full criterion. The child ACs are truncated the same way, and the resulting
similarity scores (0.14-0.28) fall below the 0.4 threshold, producing a false `stop` that blocks
`plan_complete`. This is also consistent with the earlier observation recorded on
SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63 that keeping an auxiliary item as a `wl` child made coverage report `stop`.

## Goal

Wrapped acceptance-criteria bullets are extracted whole, so the coverage review measures real
coverage rather than first-line snippets.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** `extract_acceptance_criteria()` joins continuation lines of a wrapped `- ` bullet until
  the next blank line, next bullet, or next `##` heading, and returns the full criterion text.
  *Verification:* a unit test with a multi-line wrapped AC asserts the full text is returned.
- **AC2** A regression test reproduces the observed failure: a parent with wrapped ACs and a child
  whose mapping bullet restates the *full* parent AC yields `fully_covered: True`; and the
  pre-fix behaviour (first-line-only) is covered by an explicit test asserting the fix (not by
  asserting the bug).
- **AC3** Backwards compatibility: descriptions whose ACs are already single-line return identical
  results (`skill/shared/tests/test_tree_coverage.py` stays green, extended as needed).
- **AC4** The similarity threshold semantics are documented in the module docstring: tokens are
  lowercased/punctuation-stripped, and parent/child AC text is compared as whole criteria.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` — `extract_acceptance_criteria`, `compute_coverage`, `resolve_coverage_gaps`.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_tree_coverage.py` — regression tests.
- `docs/dev/plan-skill-reference.md` — note the mapping convention (child ACs should restate the
  parent criterion they cover).

## Notes

- Discovered during planning of SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63. Workaround applied in that plan: each child
  carries an explicit `Covers parent ACn — ...` bullet restating the parent AC's first line, which
  lifts the Jaccard score to ~0.8 and lets the review return `proceed` (100%).
- A real fix should not require the workaround wording.

- **discovered-from:** SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63

# Stale local branch `origin/dev` causes ambiguous ref resolution in changed-scope test selection

## Problem

The `run_tests.py` changed-file detection defaults to the unqualified ref `origin/dev`. When a local branch shadows a remote-tracking ref (e.g. `refs/heads/origin/dev` coexisting with `refs/remotes/origin/dev`), `git merge-base origin/dev HEAD` resolves to the wrong ref, causing full-repository diffs and breaking changed-scope test selection.

The stale local branch was cleaned up in SA-0MUG216UP008821M, but the code remains fragile — any future local branch creation with an `origin/` prefix would re-trigger the ambiguity.

## Users

- **Implementation agents** running `implement.py finish` / `run_tests.py --scope changed` — rely on correct changed-file detection.
- **Operators / CI** — depend on efficient test runs that only exercise changed code.

### Example user stories

- As an implementation agent, when `run_tests.py` detects changed files, I want the base ref to resolve unambiguously so my test scope is correct.
- As an operator, I want the changed-scope tooling to be immune to local branch shadowing hazards — a future mistake must not silently break test selection.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1** — All changed-scope code paths in `run_tests.py` that accept a `base_ref` default use fully-qualified `refs/remotes/origin/dev` instead of the unqualified `origin/dev`.
- [ ] **AC2** — `_resolve_merge_base()` detects and warns when an unqualified `origin/<branch>` is ambiguous (both local branch and remote-tracking ref exist) and resolves to the correct remote-tracking ref.
- [ ] **AC3** — A regression test covers the scenario where a local branch shadows `origin/<branch>`, verifying that changed-scope detection still resolves correctly.
- [ ] **AC4** — Full project test suite passes with the new changes.
- [ ] **AC5** — Documentation referencing the changed-scope base-ref default is updated: `skill/test/SKILL.md` (`--target-branch` default note) and `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` (`--target-branch` section).

## Constraints

- No new runtime dependencies; reuse existing git helpers.
- Preserve backward compatibility: `--base` / `--target-branch` CLI flags must still accept unqualified names.
- All written output in UK English.

## Existing state

- `run_tests.py` `base_ref` defaults to `"origin/dev"` in `_run_scope_changed()`, `main()`, `run_changed()`, and `run_tests_with_scope()` — lines 233, 549, 1473, 1680, 1995, 2241.
- `_resolve_merge_base()` (line 276) tries `base_ref`, then `dev`, then `HEAD~1` as fallbacks but does not detect ambiguity.
- The stale local branch `refs/heads/origin/dev` was deleted in SA-0MUG216UP008821M.
- `implement.py`'s fix (SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1) already uses `refs/remotes/origin/<parent>` — pattern to follow.

## Desired change

1. Change the default `base_ref` value from `"origin/dev"` to `"refs/remotes/origin/dev"` in all relevant function signatures.
2. Enhance `_resolve_merge_base()` to detect ambiguity: when the default base ref is `origin/<branch>`, check whether both `refs/heads/origin/<branch>` and `refs/remotes/origin/<branch>` exist. If so, warn and prefer `refs/remotes/origin/<branch>`.
3. Add regression tests in `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py` covering the shadowing scenario.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — change default `base_ref` values; enhance `_resolve_merge_base()`.
- `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py` — new regression tests for AC2/AC3 (existing test file; add shadowing regression tests here).

## Related work

- **SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1** — implement.py finish: post-push local parent sync; already uses fully-qualified refs to avoid this hazard.
- **SA-0MUG216UP008821M** — fixture artefact cleanup; already removed the stale `refs/heads/origin/dev` branch.
- **SA-0MUH1MJL6003767Q** — companion discovered issue from the same session.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk:** Changing the default base ref from `origin/dev` to `refs/remotes/origin/dev` could break external tooling that passes `origin/dev` explicitly — mitigate: the CLI flags accept the value as-is, only the default changes.
- **Risk:** The ambiguity detection in `_resolve_merge_base()` adds a `git for-each-ref` call per invocation — negligible overhead (~ms).
- **Risk (scope creep):** Hardening every other script that uses `origin/<branch>` (e.g. `implement.py` helpers) is tracked in SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1; only `run_tests.py` is in scope here.
- **Assumption:** No legitimate local branches should use the `origin/` prefix — git convention reserves `origin/` for remote-tracking refs.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Should we also harden other scripts that use `origin/<branch>`?** — **Answer (agent research):** `implement.py` already hardened in SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1. Other scripts (e.g. `skill/audit/`) use `origin/dev` but not in the changed-scope context — out of scope.
- **Q: Is the stale branch still present?** — **Answer (agent research):** No — deleted in SA-0MUG216UP008821M (commit e36dd153). The AC about triaging the branch is satisfied by that cleanup.

# Intake Brief: Add linter rule-code prefix mappings for DTZ, PLW, and other unknown types

**Work Item:** SA-0MUIBBY3U005JBC4

---

## Problem

The `_linter_code_to_smell_type` function in `skill/refactor/smell_detection.py` maps ruff rule-code prefixes to smell types, but several common prefixes are missing from the mapping. This causes findings from these rules to be classified as `unknown`, losing valuable categorisation in the refactor scan output.

A full-project scan on 2026-09-26 found 5 findings — DTZ001 and PLW1510 — all mapped to `unknown`.

| Code Prefix | Linter Plugin / Category | Current Mapping | Suggested Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| DTZ | flake8-datetimez (datetime without tzinfo) | unknown | security |
| PLW | pylint warning (e.g. PLW1510: subprocess.run without check) | unknown | bug_risk |

## Users

- **Refactor scan consumer:** When running `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py`, findings are categorised by smell type to group and prioritise issues. `unknown` smell types make it harder to triage and act on findings.
- **Developer reviewing refactor output:** Meaningful smell types help developers understand the nature of each finding without drilling into the raw rule code.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1:** `DTZ` prefix maps to `security` smell type in `_linter_code_to_smell_type`.
2. **AC2:** `PLW` prefix maps to `bug_risk` smell type in `_linter_code_to_smell_type`.
3. **AC3:** Unit tests in `tests/test_refactor/test_smell_detection.py` cover the new DTZ and PLW mappings.
4. **AC4:** Re-running the refactor scan on affected files produces findings with proper smell types (not `unknown`) for DTZ and PLW codes. (Scoped to the prefixes being added — not a guarantee against all possible unknown prefixes in the ruff ecosystem.)

## Constraints

- Changes are confined to `skill/refactor/smell_detection.py` and the corresponding test file.
- The fix must not alter the existing mapping for other prefixes (F, E, W, PL, etc.).
- The `_classify_ruff` function in `skill/code_review/scripts/linter_runner.py` uses a separate severity mapping (`_RUFF_SEVERITY_MAP`) — this is unaffected as DTZ and PLW severity already resolve to defaults (medium).

## Existing State

- `skill/refactor/smell_detection.py` line ~556 contains a dict mapping 14 ruff prefixes (F, E, W, D, N, C, UP, ANN, S, B, SIM, T20, PL, RUF) to smell type strings.
- Prefix extraction collects all leading alphabetic characters from the rule code (e.g. `PLW1510` → `PLW`).
- The lookup first tries the exact prefix, then falls back to `prefix[0]` if the first character is F, E, or W.
- `skill/code_review/scripts/linter_runner.py` contains a separate `_RUFF_SEVERITY_MAP` for severity classification (not smell type). DTZ falls through to "D" (medium), PLW falls through to default "medium".

## Desired Change

1. Add `DTZ: "security"` to the mapping — datetime without timezone is a security concern (SA-0MSBZ1W58009PVAL, SA-0MSBZ1QWI005YJIN, SA-0MSBZ1TVE004VBJG confirm real DTZ findings exist in the codebase).
2. Add `PLW: "bug_risk"` to the mapping — pylint warnings often indicate potential bugs (PLW1510: subprocess.run without check).
3. Add `PLE: "bug_risk"` for pylint errors and `PLR: "simplification"` for pylint refactor suggestions, completing the pylint family mapping to avoid future `unknown` findings.

## Risks

- `security` and `bug_risk` are valid return values from `_linter_code_to_smell_type` but are not listed in `DEFAULT_RULES["smell_types"]`. Other code may filter against this list.
  - **Mitigation:** These values are already used by existing mappings (S → `security`, B → `bug_risk`). No code change is needed.
- Other ruff prefixes (e.g. PTH, TCH, FA) may surface as `unknown` in future scans.
  - **Mitigation:** These can be added incrementally as they appear; the pylint family is now fully covered.
- The description's original backtick-enclosed text was stripped during storage, making the description partially unreadable.
  - **Mitigation:** This brief restores all code references with proper Markdown formatting.

## Assumptions made during intake (not requiring producer approval):

- DTZ → `security`: accepted as per the description's rationale and confirmed by related work items tracking DTZ findings.
- PLW → `bug_risk`: accepted as per the description's rationale.
- PLE → `bug_risk` and PLR → `simplification`: included as part of the pylint family to maximise AC4 coverage.
- AC4 is scoped to the prefixes being fixed (DTZ, PLW, and optionally PLE, PLR), not to every possible unknown prefix in the ecosystem.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/refactor/smell_detection.py` — `_linter_code_to_smell_type` function: add 3–5 new entries to the `mapping` dict.
- `tests/test_refactor/test_smell_detection.py` — add tests for the new prefix mappings (DTZ, PLW, PLE, PLR).

## Related Work

- **SA-0MQA7190M0058Y3R** – Smell Detection Engine (completed) — foundational work for smell detection.
- **SA-0MSBZ1W58009PVAL** — DTZ001 finding (datetime.datetime() without tzinfo).
- **SA-0MSBZ1QWI005YJIN** — DTZ005 finding (datetime.datetime.now() without tz).
- **SA-0MSBZ1TVE004VBJG** — DTZ006 finding (datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp() without tz).
- **SA-0MTYJ4S6W004T4V2** — PLW1510 finding (subprocess.run without check, completed).
- **SA-0MPPI0GG4006IQUF** – Add Karpathy-inspired coding disciplines (completed, tangential).
- **SA-0MQPP6TFJ008LU1N** – wl close recovery path (completed, tangential).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview conducted — seed context was deemed sufficient to draft a clear brief. Assumptions documented above.

# implement.py parent ignores do-not-delegate and leaves stale worktree branches

## Problem statement

The global implement skill's parent phase (`implement.py parent`, `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`) has two gaps that make an epic loop when a child is externally blocked: it selects `do-not-delegate`-tagged children as implementable (so every dispatch re-attempts a guarded child), and a failed/aborted `start` leaves the child's feature branch behind so every subsequent `start` fails with a cryptic "Failed to create worktree" error.

## Users

- **Automated dispatchers (herdr downtime worker)** that run `implement.py parent <epic>` unattended — they need guarded children skipped and reported, not re-attempted on every cycle.
- **Operators** running `implement.py start` / `implement.py abort` on a child — they need a clear stale-branch diagnostic with a recovery path instead of a generic failure.
- Example story: *As the herdr dispatcher, when an epic's only remaining startable child is `do-not-delegate` (externally blocked), `implement.py parent` reports it as guarded and starts the next genuinely startable sibling — or stops cleanly reporting "no startable child" — rather than re-selecting the guarded child.*
- Example story: *As an operator whose earlier `start` aborted, re-running `implement.py start <child>` either resumes cleanly from the existing branch or tells me exactly which stale branch to delete.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Parent skips guarded children.** `implement.py parent` treats a child tagged `do-not-delegate` as not startable: `_classify_child` returns a dedicated guarded classification (e.g. `skip-do-not-delegate`), and both `_next_child_to_implement` and the `phase_parent` child loop skip it, reporting it in the parent report with a distinct action (e.g. `"skipped-do-not-delegate"`) and no dependency-`blocked` masking. Guarded children are never started, claimed, or re-attempted by `parent`; startable siblings still proceed.
- [ ] **AC2 — Explicit override still works.** Direct `implement.py start <child>` / `drive <child>` on a `do-not-delegate` child continues to work (that explicit invocation is the documented override); only automatic parent recursion is gated.
- [ ] **AC3 — Stale branch handled actionably.** When the target child branch (`wl-<id>-<slug>`) already exists, `phase_start` no longer fails generically: it either reuses the existing worktree/branch (when that branch is at, or fast-forwardable from, the parent branch) or fails with an actionable error naming the stale branch and the recovery command. `git_worktree_add`'s boolean-only contract is extended so the caller can distinguish "branch exists" from other failures.
- [ ] **AC4 — Failed/aborted start leaves no stale branch.** A `start` that fails after creating the branch cleans up the branch it created; `phase_abort` removes the abandoned feature branch (with a guarded delete — never force-deleting a branch with unmerged commits that are the only copy) and reports what it removed.
- [ ] **AC5 — Regression tests.** Unit tests cover: `_classify_child` / `_next_child_to_implement` with `do-not-delegate` children (guarded skipped, siblings still selected, override path unaffected) and `git_worktree_add` / `phase_start` stale-branch handling (reuse, fast-forward, actionable error, cleanup). Existing parent-recursion/dependency test suites still pass.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation.** `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (parent-phase and abort sections) and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` document guarded-child reporting and stale-branch reuse/recovery, including code comments for the new classification action.
- [ ] **AC7 — Full suite green.** The full project test suite passes with the new changes (enforced at the dev-push gate).

## Constraints

- Agent-infrastructure code owned by this repository: all edits land in `skill/implement/` here; never edit the installed copy (`~/.pi/agent/skills/...`) or an AI_Hell worktree.
- Idempotence: re-running `implement.py parent` must not create duplicate branches, duplicate worktrees, or duplicate comments, and must not reset a guarded child's status/stage.
- Never clobber another agent's in-progress claim (existing `skip-in-progress` behaviour is preserved).
- Guardedness must be distinguishable from dependency-blocking in the report so operators can see *why* a child did not start.
- The branch-cleanup path must never delete the only copy of a child's commits (no blind `git branch -D`).
- Do not relax the existing main-checkout placement guard, stash-hygiene gate, or code-freeze gate.

## Existing state

- `_classify_child` (implement.py ~line 872) returns only `skip-terminal`, `skip-in-progress`, or `implement`; it inspects `status` and `deletedBy` only — it never looks at `tags`. `wl show <id> --children --json` does expose each child's `tags`, so `do-not-delegate` is readable without new plumbing.
- `_next_child_to_implement` (~line 963) and the `phase_parent` child loop (~line 5730+) both rely on `_classify_child`, so a single classification change propagates to both.
- `git_worktree_add` (~line 1826) runs `git worktree add --track -b <branch> <path> <parent_branch>` and returns a bare `bool`; `git worktree add -b` fails when the branch already exists.
- `phase_start` (~line 4254) reuses an existing worktree via `_is_worktree` (SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9) but, when no worktree exists and the branch does, it reports `Failed to create worktree at ...` and only resets status to `open` — the branch survives.
- `phase_abort` (~line 5406) calls `_remove_worktree` (which removes the directory but never the branch), so the branch survives an abort and poisons the next `start`.
- No `do-not-delegate` handling exists anywhere in `implement.py` today (grep confirms); the herdr dispatcher honours the tag, the implement parent phase does not.
- Sibling item `SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1` (completed) already added parent-branch (`dev`) refresh before worktree creation (step 6.5 `_sync_parent_branch`); this item concerns the *child* branch already existing, which that work does not address.

## Desired change

1. Add `do-not-delegate` awareness to `_classify_child`, surface it as a distinct action in the `phase_parent` report, and skip those children in both selection paths.
2. Make `phase_start`/`git_worktree_add` branch-aware: detect an existing child branch, reuse it when safe (identical to / fast-forwardable from the parent branch), otherwise fail with the branch name and recovery command.
3. Clean up the branch a failed `start` created, and delete the abandoned branch on `phase_abort` when it is safe to do so.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_classify_child`, `_next_child_to_implement`, `phase_parent` (classification report + child loop), `git_worktree_add`, `phase_start` (step 7 worktree creation), `phase_abort`
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — document guarded-child behaviour and stale-branch recovery
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — reference documentation for the new classification action and branch handling
- `tests/test_implement_parent_dependency.py`, `tests/test_implement_parent_loop.py`, `tests/test_implement_parent_recursion.py` — existing parent-phase suites to extend
- `tests/test_implement_start_resume.py`, `tests/test_implement_abort_safety.py` — existing start/abort suites to extend for stale-branch handling

## Related work

- **SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876** — `implement.py parent` ignores the `do-not-delegate` tag when selecting the next child (open). The `do-not-delegate`-only subset of this item, retained to preserve the original report; its description states it should be closed as duplicate/absorbed once this item is resolved.
- **SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1** — `implement.py finish` leaves local `dev` behind after pushing to remote `dev` (completed). Related theme: stale base for the *next* child; that item fixed the parent-branch refresh, not the child-branch-already-exists failure.
- **SA-0MQP8K03I007DVMM** — Implement skill safety gate should account for git worktrees (completed). Related worktree lifecycle work; different gate (dirty-tree safety), no overlap with either gap here.
- **SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9** — idempotent `start` that reuses an existing worktree (referenced in code); this item extends that idempotence to the branch-already-exists-no-worktree case.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (override semantics):** "unless explicitly overridden" means a direct `implement.py start`/`drive <child>` invocation, which remains the escape hatch; `parent` gets no override flag. If a `parent`-level override flag is wanted, that is an addition, not a change to AC1/AC2.
- **Risk — branch reuse ambiguity:** a stale branch may contain real partial work. Mitigation: reuse only when identical to or fast-forwardable from the parent branch; otherwise fail with instructions and never auto-delete commits.
- **Risk — false guard detection:** if the tag is written differently in another worklog (e.g. a boolean field rather than a `tags` entry), classification could miss it. Mitigation: read the same shape the herdr dispatcher uses (`tags` contains `do-not-delegate`) and add a test fixture pinning that shape.
- **Risk — scope creep into herdr:** the dispatcher's own selection logic is out of scope; this item covers `implement.py` only.
- **Risk — parent stalls silently:** if every remaining child is guarded, `parent` must report "no startable child (N guarded)" rather than a bare "nothing to do". Covered by AC1's report requirement.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview questions were required: the relocated report (`relocated-from:AH-0MUVRNAU5005PEUE`) already states the problem, expected behaviour, and scope, and code inspection of `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` confirmed every claim (classification paths, `git_worktree_add`'s `-b` flag, `phase_start` failure handling, `phase_abort` branch retention). One design reading is recorded as an assumption under **Risks & assumptions** ("explicitly overridden" = direct `start`/`drive` of the child).

- Q (self-resolved): "Does `wl show --children --json` expose child tags so `do-not-delegate` is detectable?" — Answer (Map): Yes; the child dict carries `tags`, and existing local worklog data stores the tag as `"tags":["do-not-delegate"]`. Source: `worklog-data.jsonl` inspection + `wl update --help` (`--do-not-delegate` flag).
- Q (self-resolved): "Is the stale-branch failure already fixed by the parent-branch refresh?" — Answer (Map): No; `SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1` refreshes the parent branch (`dev`) before worktree creation, but `git worktree add -b` still fails when the child's own branch already exists. Source: `phase_start` step 6.5 / step 7 code.

## Related work (automated report, find-related)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MM8SJKC31N0PQ55** – Resolve stale container-dispatch branches and close associated work items (completed) — directly relevant: prior branch-staleness incident and its manual cleanup.
- **SA-0MSKB6VJA005N43F** – Audit: parent-first child pass-through (audit parent only first) (completed) — parent-phase traversal behaviour.
- **SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T** – implement skill: /skill:implement <parent-id> must automatically implement children and blockers in the chain (completed) — origin of the parent recursion this item modifies.

### Repository file matches
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: abort, branch, child, classify, delegate, guarded, parent, stale, startable, worktree
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: branch, child, classify, guarded, parent, worktree (audit's parent recursion shares classification vocabulary)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: branch, child, classify, guarded, parent, worktree

# Commit hooks exec a hard-coded per-user path → `git worktree add` and `wl sync` fail

## Problem statement

The committed hooks `.githooks/post-checkout`, `.githooks/post-merge` and
`.githooks/post-rewrite` unconditionally `exec` the absolute path
`/home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`. That path is
per-user and machine-specific, so on any host where it is absent (a different
username, a clean machine, CI) every checkout, merge and `git worktree add` in
this repository exits 127 — which in turn breaks `wl sync` (its
temporary-worktree merge) and `implement.py start`/`finish` worktree creation.
The repository already commits the real script as `.githooks/worklog-post-pull`,
but no wrapper references it.

## Reproduction

```sh
cd /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents
# The wrapper hard-codes an absolute path, so the failure is independent of
# $HOME. Simulate a host where that path does not exist by moving the central
# symlink aside for one command (restore it afterwards):
LINK=$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull
mv "$LINK" "$LINK.bak"
git worktree add --detach /tmp/sa-wt-repro HEAD
mv "$LINK.bak" "$LINK"
# → .githooks/post-checkout: 4: exec: /home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull: not found
# → rc=127 (verified during intake)
```

On the current agent host the immediate trigger is masked because
`/home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull` exists as a symlink to
this repo's committed script (installed by `scripts/install_pi.sh`), so normal
runs here exit 0 ("worklog: sync failed or not initialized; continuing"). The
defect is therefore latent on this host and reproduces on every host or clean
clone where that absolute path is absent.

## Users

- **AI agent driving `/skill:implement`** — needs `implement.py start`/`finish`
  to create worktrees without a hook failure aborting the run.
  Story: *As an implementing agent, when I start work on an item, the worktree
  is created successfully even though the machine has no central hook install.*
- **Agent or developer running `wl sync`** — needs the sync push to complete.
  Story: *As an agent publishing Worklog data, `wl sync` completes its push
  step on a clean clone without setting `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1` or
  `core.hooksPath=/dev/null`.*
- **Developer on a second machine / CI checkout** — needs the committed hooks
  to be portable.
  Story: *As a developer whose username is not `rgardler`, cloning and
  checking out this repository does not emit `exec: ... not found`.*
- **Framework maintainer** — needs the behaviour pinned by a regression test.
  Story: *As a maintainer of the agent framework, I need a test that fails if a
  committed hook regains a hard-coded per-user path.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **No hard-coded per-user path.** The three wrappers
      (`.githooks/post-checkout`, `post-merge`, `post-rewrite`) resolve the
      post-pull script without any absolute `/home/<user>` path: they first try
      the repository-relative `<toplevel>/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`, then
      `$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`, and when neither exists
      they print one clear line to stderr and exit 0 (never 127, never a silent
      failure).
- [ ] **Regression test proving `git worktree add` succeeds.** A hermetic test
      asserts (a) the committed wrappers contain no absolute `/home/<user>` or
      other machine-specific path; (b) in a temp repository built from the
      committed `.githooks/` with `core.hooksPath=.githooks`, a sandboxed
      `$HOME` that has no `.config/pi`, and a stubbed `wl` on `PATH`,
      `git worktree add --detach <tmp> HEAD` exits 0, emits no
      `exec: ... not found`, and reaches the repo-relative
      `.githooks/worklog-post-pull`; and (c) the same setup with
      `worklog-post-pull` absent takes the graceful no-op path (one stderr
      notice naming the attempted locations, `rc=0`, no sync attempted).
- [ ] **`wl sync` completes its push step** in this repository on a host
      without the central hook install (sandboxed `$HOME`), without the
      `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1` / `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` workaround.
- [ ] **Hooks cannot recurse.** A hook-triggered sync from `wl`'s own
      `.worklog/tmp-worktree-*` (and from a linked worktree) exits before
      calling `wl sync`, matching the guards already present in the sibling
      ContextHub/AI_Hell hooks.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries —
      specifically replacing the portability caveat in `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md`
      and updating the `install_pi.sh` fail-open warning to match the new hook
      behaviour.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Hooks are POSIX `sh` executed by git; they must stay dependency-free (no
  python, no network) and fast, because they run on every checkout/merge.
- `$HOME` and `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` must both be treated as
  best-effort: hook execution inherits git's environment, and earlier incidents
  (SA-0MV0G9BF7008S01K, SA-0MUIZSXEY008NGR8) showed `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_*` pollution
  in spawned sessions. Every resolution step fails open.
- Keep the shared-script model (one implementation in
  `.githooks/worklog-post-pull`) rather than inlining a copy into each wrapper;
  the sibling repositories' self-contained hooks are precedent for the guards,
  not for duplicating sync logic.
- Do not touch the `pre-push` hook behaviour (`worklog:pre-push-hook:v3`) or the
  full-suite gate; this item changes only the post-pull chain.
- Sibling project checkouts (`ContentCreator`, `ContextHub`, `AI_Hell`) are out
  of scope; the ContextHub/AI_Hell copies are reference implementations only,
  and any divergence found there becomes a linked follow-up item.
- Build → test → commit order; no ad-hoc `pytest` — use the test skill /
  `run_tests.py`.
- Preserve the existing bypass variables (`WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1`,
  `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1`) and their documented semantics.

## Existing state (verified during intake)

- The three wrappers are 184-byte files with header
  `worklog:post-pull-hook:v1` and a single
  `exec "/home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull" "$@"` line
  (`.githooks/post-checkout`, `post-merge`, `post-rewrite`).
- `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` **is committed** (514 bytes; runs `wl sync`,
  honours `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1`, fail-open when `wl` is absent). Nothing
  in the repository invokes it: `rg worklog-post-pull` finds only the wrappers'
  hard-coded path, `scripts/install_pi.sh` (central install), one test file and
  the docs.
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` installs the central script as an executable symlink
  to the repo copy (`create_symlink`, idempotent, `PI_SKIP_HOOK_INSTALL=1`
  gated) and then emits a **warning only** when a project's committed wrapper
  does not reference that central path. The warning does not fix the wrapper.
- `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` (~lines 100–120) documents the delegation and
  carries a "Portability caveat (SA-0MVK1Q30O0067NXX)" paragraph describing
  exactly this defect as unresolved.
- Sibling repositories (`ContextHub`, `AI_Hell`) ship
  self-contained `post-checkout`/`worklog-post-pull` hooks that (a) skip
  `*tmp-worktree-*` paths and (b) skip linked worktrees
  (`git rev-parse --git-dir` vs `--git-common-dir`). The SorraAgents copy of
  `worklog-post-pull` lacks both guards. (`ContentCreator` is reported in the
  consolidated duplicate item to have the same self-contained pattern, but that
  checkout is not present on this host, so it was not verified directly.)
- Verified on this host: `git worktree add --detach /tmp/sa-wt-intake-check HEAD`
  now exits 0 ("worklog: sync failed or not initialized; continuing") because
  the central symlink exists — the hard-coded path is what breaks elsewhere.
- `tests/test_install_pi_post_pull_hook.py` covers the *installer* and writes
  its own synthetic hooks; no test asserts the content or behaviour of this
  repository's committed wrappers.
- `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py` and `tests/test_pre_push_hook_fallback.py`
  cover the pre-push wiring only.

## Desired change

1. Rewrite the three wrappers to resolve the post-pull script in this order:
   repository-relative (via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, falling back to
   `dirname "$0"`), then `$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`, then a
   single-line stderr notice + `exit 0`. No literal `/home/<user>` anywhere.
2. Add the `*tmp-worktree-*` and linked-worktree guards to
   `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` so a hook-triggered sync cannot nest inside
   `wl sync`'s own temporary worktree, mirroring the sibling implementations.
3. Update the `install_pi.sh` portability warning to reflect the fixed
   behaviour (warning remains a guard for *forked/older* wrappers only).
4. Replace the docs caveat with the actual resolution order and the no-op
   behaviour; document the bypass variables.
5. Add the hermetic regression test described in the ACs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.githooks/post-checkout`, `.githooks/post-merge`, `.githooks/post-rewrite` — replace the hard-coded `exec` with portable resolution + graceful no-op.
- `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` — add tmp-worktree and linked-worktree guards; keep `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL` bypass.
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — adjust the fail-open portability warning/message to the new contract.
- `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` — replace the portability caveat with the resolution order and no-op semantics.
- `tests/test_githooks_portability.py` — new hermetic regression tests (worktree add succeeds under a sandboxed `$HOME`; no-op path; bypass; no hard-coded `/home/<user>` in committed hooks).
- `tests/test_install_pi_post_pull_hook.py` — extend only if the installer warning contract changes.

## Related work

- `SA-0MU8CRX1X008IORP` — *Chore: install central wl post-pull hook
  (~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull) missing* (completed): installed the
  central symlink and the wrapper-to-central delegation this item now makes
  portable.
- `SA-0MVK2PK7F002LET6` — *SorraAgents committed git hooks exec a missing
  central script* (closed as duplicate of this item; its reproduction
  transcript, sibling self-contained-hook precedent and `WORKLOG_SKIP_*`
  behaviour are folded in above).
- `SA-0MV8M4OVX000QHSM` — *install_pi.sh propagates the SorraAgents-only test
  gate to non-SorraAgents projects* (completed): precedent for project-vs-framework
  hook variants in the same installer block.
- `SA-0MV0G9BF7008S01K`, `SA-0MUIZSXEY008NGR8` — hook/GIT environment
  investigations that motivate fail-open resolution.
- `SA-0MUJ2VMF7000UHCX` — pre-push git-identity guard (same hook family; do not
  regress it).
- Related docs: `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md`, `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`.
- Related files: `.githooks/pre-push` (v3 pattern for `git rev-parse`-based
  resolution), sibling `.githooks/{post-checkout,worklog-post-pull}` in
  `ContextHub`/`AI_Hell`.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** repo-relative resolution is the intended shape (the ACs allow
  either repo-relative delegation or inline logic; the repository already
  commits `.githooks/worklog-post-pull`, so reusing it is the minimal change).
- **Assumption:** keeping `$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull` as a
  second candidate preserves compatibility with framework projects whose
  wrappers are installed by `install_pi.sh`.
- **Risk:** `git rev-parse` inside a hook can be misled by `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_*`
  pollution. Mitigation: `2>/dev/null`, fall back to `dirname "$0"`, then
  `$HOME`, then no-op.
- **Risk:** a no-op can hide a broken install. Mitigation: the stderr line names
  both attempted paths and points at `scripts/install_pi.sh`.
- **Risk:** the new test could invoke real `wl` (network/sync side effects).
  Mitigation: sandboxed `$HOME`, stub `wl` on `PATH`, or assert the no-op path
  only; never perform a real sync in the test.
- **Scope-creep risk:** rewriting hooks in sibling repositories, redesigning
  `wl sync`, or changing the pre-push gate are out of scope; record as linked
  follow-up items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were asked in this intake: the seed brief, the
reproduction transcript from the consolidated duplicate, and repository
inspection supplied enough detail to draft an unambiguous brief.

Research performed (evidence links):

- Q (self-resolved): "Does the repository already contain the post-pull
  script?" — Answer: **yes**, `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` is committed
  (514 bytes) but unreferenced by the wrappers. Evidence: `rg worklog-post-pull`;
  file contents.
- Q (self-resolved): "Why does the failure not appear on this host?" — Answer:
  the wrappers hard-code `/home/rgardler`, and on this host the
  `scripts/install_pi.sh` install (`SA-0MU8CRX1X008IORP`) provides that exact
  path as a symlink to the repo script, so checkout succeeds and the defect is
  latent. Removing the symlink for one command reproduces `rc=127`; changing
  `$HOME` alone does not, because the path is absolute. Evidence:
  `mv …/worklog-post-pull …; git worktree add …; mv back` (verified during
  intake), `ls -la ~/.config/pi/.githooks`.
- Q (self-resolved): "Is there a precedent implementation?" — Answer: **yes**,
  `ContextHub` and `AI_Hell` ship self-contained post-checkout hooks with
  `*tmp-worktree-*` and linked-worktree guards. Evidence: sibling `.githooks/`
  contents (`ContentCreator` not present on this host).
- Q (self-resolved): "Is the defect already tested?" — Answer: **no**.
  `tests/test_install_pi_post_pull_hook.py` tests the installer with synthetic
  hooks; nothing asserts the committed wrappers. Evidence: `rg` over `tests/`.
- Duplicate check performed: `wl search "post-pull hook"` / `"worklog hook"`
  found `SA-0MVK2PK7F002LET6` (same defect), closed as a duplicate of this item;
  no other overlapping open or completed item found.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MVK2PK7F002LET6** – SorraAgents committed git hooks exec a missing central script (~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull) (completed)
- **SA-0MU8CRX1X008IORP** – Chore: install central wl post-pull hook (~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull) missing (completed)
- **SA-0MV0G9BF7008S01K** – GIT_DIR evidence: trace non-destructive env propagation path (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: aborting, absent, absolute, acceptance, acs (+344 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: absent, absolute, acceptance, acs, actual (+314 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: aborting, absent, absolute, actual, add (+294 more)
## Plan (2026-10-27)

**Decision: single leaf item — no child decomposition.** The change is one
atomic fix to a small, tightly-coupled hook contract (three wrappers + the
script they exec + installer wiring + docs) estimated **Small / Medium**
(5.42h expected). Splitting it into child items would leave intermediate
commits with a half-portable hook chain and a red suite — the committed suite
must be green at every commit — so the work is implemented as one vertical
slice that cuts through hooks, installer, tests and docs.

Rationale recorded per the plan skill's step 5 (phasing not required for an
item of this size; documented rather than silently skipped).

**Duplicate check:** `wl search "post-pull hook" | "worklog hook" |
"githooks portability" | "worktree add 127"` found no open item covering these
ACs. `SA-0MVK2PK7F002LET6` is the already-closed duplicate of this item;
`SA-0MU8CRX1X008IORP` (completed) installed the central symlink;
`SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1` (open) is precedent for the *local-then-global
resolution* pattern in the pre-push hook and stays a separate item.

### Implementation order (test-first; suite green at each commit)

1. **Tests first** — add `tests/test_githooks_portability.py`, hermetic and
   offline, covering:
   - (a) static: no committed wrapper contains `/home/<user>` or another
     machine-specific absolute path (guards AC1);
   - (b) temp repository built from the committed `.githooks/` with
     `core.hooksPath=.githooks`, a sandboxed `$HOME` with no `.config/pi`, and
     a stub `wl` on `PATH` → `git worktree add --detach` exits 0, prints no
     `exec: ... not found`, and the repo-relative
     `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` is the script that ran (marker file);
   - (c) same setup with `worklog-post-pull` removed → `rc=0`, exactly one
     stderr notice naming both attempted locations, stub `wl` never invoked;
   - (d) `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1` bypasses the sync;
   - (e) recursion guards: `PWD` containing `tmp-worktree-`, and a linked
     worktree (`--git-dir` ≠ `--git-common-dir`), both exit before `wl sync`.
2. **Rewrite the three wrappers** (`.githooks/post-checkout`, `post-merge`,
   `post-rewrite`) to resolve `worklog-post-pull` as: repo-relative
   (`<toplevel>/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`, falling back to
   `dirname "$0"/worklog-post-pull`) → `$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/...` →
   one-line stderr notice + `exit 0`. Test for existence/executability before
   `exec` so a missing script can never produce 127. Keep the
   `worklog:post-pull-hook:v1` marker (no version bump: `install_pi.sh`
   detects wiring by content, and the sibling projects use v1 markers).
   *Commit A: tests + wrappers.*
3. **Add recursion guards** to `.githooks/worklog-post-pull`: skip
   `*tmp-worktree-*` paths and linked worktrees before the `wl sync` call,
   mirroring the ContextHub/AI_Hell copies; keep the
   `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1` bypass first.
4. **Update `scripts/install_pi.sh`**: the fail-open portability warning must
   now fire only for *legacy/foreign* wrappers (no repo-relative resolution and
   no reference to `$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`), and must no
   longer warn about this repository's fixed wrappers; refresh the explanatory
   comment block. *Commit B: guards + installer.*
5. **Docs**: replace the "Portability caveat (SA-0MVK1Q30O0067NXX)" paragraph
   in `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` with the resolution order, the no-op
   behaviour and the bypass variables. Touch
   `tests/test_install_pi_post_pull_hook.py` only if the installer warning
   contract changed. *Commit C: docs.*
6. **Verify**: changed-scope tests, then the full suite via `/skill:test`
   (AC6); capture AC3 evidence (see below). *Commit D only if fix-ups are
   needed.*

### AC → verification map

| AC | Proven by |
|----|-----------|
| No hard-coded per-user path | static scan (test 1a) + resolution/`exit 0` behaviour in tests 1b/1c |
| Regression test proves `git worktree add` succeeds | tests 1a, 1b, 1c |
| `wl sync` completes its push step without the central install | see *AC3 evidence* note |
| Hooks cannot recurse | test 1e |
| Docs updated | review diff of `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md`, comment blocks and `install_pi.sh` |
| Full suite passes | `/skill:test` full scope before the dev push |

**AC3 evidence note.** No automated test may perform a real sync (risk noted
below). Preferred proof: a hermetic temp clone with a **local bare remote** and
a sandboxed `$HOME`, running `wl sync` so its push step completes with no
network access and no `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1` / `core.hooksPath=/dev/null`
workaround. If `wl` cannot push to a local remote in that sandbox, record the
manual transcript (commands + exit codes) as a comment on this item instead —
the AC is satisfied by evidence, not necessarily by a test.

### Implementation notes

- Keep the shared-script model: the wrappers delegate; only
  `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` contains sync logic (no inlined copies).
- Survive `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_*` pollution (`SA-0MV0G9BF7008S01K`,
  `SA-0MUIZSXEY008NGR8`): every `git rev-parse` is `2>/dev/null`-guarded and
  falls through to `$HOME`, then the no-op.
- Do not touch `.githooks/pre-push` / `pre-push.v2`, the full-suite gate or the
  `worklog:pre-push-hook:v3` marker.
- Sibling checkouts (`ContextHub`, `AI_Hell`) are reference only; any
  divergence found there becomes a linked follow-up item, not an edit here.

## Plan: changelog

- **2026-10-27** — Plan applied: single-leaf decision recorded, test-first
  implementation order, AC→verification map and AC3 evidence note added;
  duplicate check performed (no overlapping open item); effort/risk reused from
  the 2026-10-23 estimate (Small / Medium, 5.42h expected); stage advanced to
  `plan_complete`.

## Appendix: Plan session (2026-10-27)

No clarifying questions were put to the producer: the intake brief plus the
files verified during this session supplied the plan inputs. Self-resolved
items (each with evidence):

- Q: "Does the repository's committed wrapper content still match the intake
  description?" — **Yes.** Each of `.githooks/post-checkout`, `post-merge` and
  `post-rewrite` is the 3-comment-line wrapper ending in
  `exec "/home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull" "$@"`; the
  committed `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` is the shared script and lacks the
  `*tmp-worktree-*` and linked-worktree guards. Evidence: file contents read
  this session.
- Q: "What exactly do the sibling guards look like, for reuse?" — **Answered**
  by `ContextHub/.githooks/worklog-post-pull` and `AI_Hell/.githooks/
  worklog-post-pull`: `case "$PWD" in *tmp-worktree-*) exit 0 ;; esac` then
  `[ "$(git rev-parse --git-dir 2>/dev/null)" != "$(git rev-parse
  --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null)" ] && exit 0`, both before the `wl sync` call.
  Precedent for the *resolution* shape comes from
  `SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1` (local-then-global runner lookup in the v3 pre-push
  hook).
- Q: "How does `install_pi.sh` currently decide to warn?" — **It greps the
  project's `.githooks/post-checkout` for the central path it just installed**
  (`scripts/install_pi.sh`, "Fail-open portability check" block). After this
  change the wrappers no longer name that absolute path first, so the check
  must be rewritten to detect *legacy* wrappers (no repo-relative resolution
  and no `$HOME` candidate) rather than deleted — recorded as step 4.
- Q: "Can the hermetic test really avoid a real sync?" — **Yes, for ACs 2, 4
  and 5**: a stub `wl` on `PATH` records invocation, so no sync runs. AC3
  needs the sync's push step, so the cost/shape is recorded as the *AC3
  evidence* note (local bare remote preferred; transcript otherwise).

OPEN QUESTION (directed to the implementer, not blocking): whether a `wl sync`
push to a **local bare remote** works inside a sandboxed `$HOME` without
credentials. If it does not, the AC3 transcript route applies — no change to
the AC text is needed and the plan is unaffected.

data.description:
# Intake Brief — Drive epic children in interactive Herdr panes

## Problem statement

`implement.py drive <parent>` (`phase_drive`, SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9) runs each
child's fresh Pi session as a **headless subprocess**:

```
pi -p "/skill:implement <child>" --approve --no-extensions
```

with `capture_output=True`. The operator therefore has:

- no view of the child session while it runs (only the parent's own progress
  lines and `wait_for_job` heartbeats);
- no ability to watch the agent work, scroll its transcript, or intervene when
  it stalls, hits an approval/question boundary, or loops;
- no evidence after a failure beyond a 5-line `_tail_lines(...)` summary of
  captured stderr/stdout;
- no per-child terminal artefact to point at during review.

An operator running an epic in Herdr already watches a grid of interactive
`π` TUI panes for other work. Drive should produce the same kind of pane —
one interactive Pi TUI session per child, opened as a sibling pane in the
caller's tab — so the epic runs *visibly*.

A headless-in-a-pane variant (option A: `pane split` + `pane run` +
exit-sentinel) was evaluated and rejected as insufficient: it shows log text,
not a browsable/typeable Pi TUI session, and offers no session-level state.

## Users

- **Operator / producer driving an epic from a Herdr-managed Pi session.**
  - *User story:* "As an operator, when I run `implement.py drive <epic>`, I
    want each child implemented in its own interactive Pi TUI pane inside the
    tab I invoked from, so I can watch progress, scroll the full transcript,
    and step in if a child stalls — without leaving my own session."
- **Reviewer / auditor.** *User story:* "As a reviewer, I want each child's
  session transcript to still be inspectable after drive finishes, so I can
  check what the agent actually did."

## Goal

`implement.py drive <parent>` opens **each** child's implementation session as
an interactive Pi TUI agent in a new pane split from the calling pane (same
tab), drives that pane's lifecycle to completion, and continues the existing
serial/blocking-order/parent-last loop — preserving session isolation,
worktree isolation, error isolation, and the recursion guard.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Pane-per-child in the caller's tab.** For each startable child, drive
   runs `herdr pane split` from the invoking pane (no `tab create`, no
   `workspace create`) with `--cwd <child worktree>` and returns the new pane
   id from `.result.pane.pane_id`; the child Pi TUI is started in that pane via
   `herdr agent start <name> --kind pi --pane <id> -- --approve
   --no-extensions` and prompted with `/skill:implement <child_id>` via
   `herdr agent prompt ... --wait`. Verified by a test that asserts the herdr
   CLI invocations (split/prompt/wait/close) and asserts no tab/workspace
   creation call is made.
2. **Driver waits on session state, not process exit.** Completion of a child
   is determined by (a) `herdr agent wait <name> --until done|blocked` for the
   pane-side signal and (b) the existing `phase_parent` re-read of the work
   item's stage as the authoritative signal. Drive never assumes an
   interactive agent process exits when the work item completes. Tests cover
   the `done`, `blocked`, and timeout transitions.
3. **Blocked children are reported, not silently abandoned.** When an agent
   reports `blocked` (approval/question UI), drive stops the chain, records the
   child id and the pane id in the JSON report (`blocked_child`,
   `blocked_pane`), leaves the pane open for the operator, and emits actionable
   text naming the pane. Tested with a fake herdr runner.
4. **No orphaned sessions:** a pane created by drive is either (a) closed once
   its child reaches a terminal stage and the child's session was clean, or
   (b) explicitly retained and reported (blocked/failed) — never leaked
   silently. Unit tests assert a close call per successful child and no close
   call for blocked/failed children.
5. **Opt-in with fail-open fallback.** Pane driving activates only when
   Herdr is detected (`HERDR_ENV=1` and a resolvable herdr binary) **and** the
   operator opted in (`--pane-sessions`, or `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_PANE_SESSIONS=1`).
   Otherwise the existing `_default_session_spawner` headless path is used
   unchanged. Tests cover herdr-absent, opt-out, and herdr-present paths.
6. **Environment isolation is preserved for pane children.** The child process
   receives `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE=1`, `IMPLEMENT_WORKTREE_PATH=<worktree>`,
   and does **not** inherit `PI_SESSION_ID` / `PI_SESSION_FILE` from the
   driving session (assert the constructed env / pane-split `--env` args and
   the `env -u` prefix). Recursion guard and per-child worktree enforcement
   continue to work inside the pane.
7. **Timeouts and iteration bounds are enforced across the new transport.**
   `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_CHILD_TIMEOUT` (and the existing per-child session bound
   `--max-child-sessions`) still bound the wait; a timeout closes the pane,
   records `reason`, and stops the chain as today. Tested with a fake clock /
   fake herdr wait returning `timeout`.
8. **Focus behaviour.** Default is `--no-focus` so the caller's focus is
   unchanged; an explicit `--focus` variant switches to each new child pane.
   Assert the flag passed to `pane split` in both modes.
9. **Report parity.** Human and `--json` reports keep the existing shape and
   gain `pane_id` per driven child plus `transport: "pane" | "headless"`; the
   final summary lists panes retained for inspection. Tests assert the new
   fields and that existing fields are unchanged (no breaking change for
   consumers of the drive report).
10. **Docs.** `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (drive section) and
    `skill/implement/SKILL.md` Step 6.1 document: pane-per-child behaviour, the
    opt-in flag/env var, focus behaviour, blocked-child handling (which pane to
    look at, and that it is intentionally left open), and the headless fallback
    for non-Herdr/automated callers.
11. **Build, tests, and full suite.** Changed-scope tests pass before commit;
    the dev-push full-suite gate is green.

## Design sketch (non-binding)

- Add `_pane_session_spawner(child_id, worktree_path, timeout, env, verbose)`
  next to `_default_session_spawner`, returning the same
  `{"success", "returncode", "reason"}` shape plus `pane_id`.
- Extract herdr CLI calls into a small injectable helper (reuse the fail-open
  style of `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py`; do not duplicate its `HERDR_BIN_PATH`
  resolution logic — reuse or import it) so tests fake the CLI boundary with
  no live Herdr.
- In `phase_drive`, select the spawner by transport: existing injection point
  (`spawn_session`) already allows tests to bypass either; the CLI path chooses
  pane vs headless from the opt-in + detection check.
- Agent naming: `drive-<child-id-lowercased>` (herdr names must match
  `[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}`, unique among live agents) — truncation/validation
  must be tested.
- Pane labelling: on completion/failure, set the pane title via the existing
  `herdr_pane.update_pane_title(status, pane_id=...)` helper so the retained
  pane carries its verdict.

## Constraints

- Do not change the session-per-child rule (SA-0MTLCCIPU0050Q52), worktree
  isolation, dependency ordering, or parent-advanced-last semantics — all live
  above the spawner.
- Do not change `_default_session_spawner` behaviour for automated callers
  (downtime worker, audit dispatch, CI): headless `pi -p` must remain the
  default outside Herdr.
- No edits to the repo-external Herdr agent skill or the installed
  `~/.pi/agent/extensions/` files (herdr-managed).
- `herdr agent start` requires the pane to be at an interactive shell prompt;
  the implementation must handle `agent_not_ready` (retry within the existing
  timeout or fail with a reported reason), not crash.
- Herdr CLI failures must be fail-open at the boundary (recorded reason,
  chain stops cleanly) — never leave the epic in an unrecoverable state.

## Risks & mitigations

- **Loss of the process-exit completion signal.** An interactive TUI session
  does not exit when the work item completes, so completion must come from
  wl stage + `agent wait`. *Mitigation:* AC 2 makes `phase_parent` the
  authority (it already is) and `agent wait` only a fast-path; covered by tests.
- **Pane/session leakage.** Panes and interactive agents persist after drive
  ends. *Mitigation:* AC 4 explicit close-or-report rule, plus pane-title
  verdict marking for retained panes.
- **Serial drive + visible panes can be noisy.** One pane open at a time,
  closed on success. *Mitigation:* documented; failure/blocked panes retained
  deliberately.
- **Herdr API drift** (JSON shapes, kind list, name rules). *Mitigation:*
  single injected helper for CLI calls; parse ids defensively; fail open.
- **Approval prompts could block an unattended epic.** *Mitigation:* start
  with `--approve` and treat `blocked` as an explicit, reported stop (AC 3).

## Existing state

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_drive`, `phase_parent`,
  `_child_session_env`, `_default_session_spawner`, `_resolve_child_session_timeout`,
  `_resolve_pi_bin`, `_emit_phase_report`; `--max-child-sessions` and
  `--child-timeout` CLI flags; `spawn_session` injection point.
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py` — deterministic orchestration tests with
  `ScriptedParent` / `RecordingSpawner`; `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_child_session.py`
  — spawer/env tests.
- `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py` — fail-open Herdr CLI helper (`HERDR_BIN_PATH`,
  `pane list`/`pane rename`, status prefix/truncation, `update_pane_title`).
- Herdr CLI surface (verified against the installed binary): `pane split
  --current --direction right|down --cwd --env --no-focus`, `pane run`,
  `pane wait-output`, `pane read`, `pane close`, `pane rename`,
  `agent start <name> --kind pi --pane <id> [-- args]`, `agent prompt
  <target> <text> --wait [--until] [--timeout]`, `agent wait`, `agent get`,
  `agent list`, `agent read`. Caller context env: `HERDR_ENV`,
  `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, `HERDR_TAB_ID`, `HERDR_PANE_ID`.

## Appendix: decisions from the discovery conversation

- Transport choice: **option B** (interactive Pi TUI agent in a pane) over
  option A (headless `pi -p` run in a pane, exit-sentinel + `pane read`).
  Rationale recorded: option A shows log text only; B gives a browsable,
  typeable session and Herdr's lifecycle states, at the cost of replacing the
  process-exit completion signal with wl-stage + `agent wait` (AC 2).
- Opt-in rather than default: automated callers (downtime worker, audit
  dispatch, CI) have no Herdr and must keep the headless path (AC 5).
- Forked-decision for planning: whether to factor the herdr CLI boundary into a
  shared module (`skill/shared/`) or keep it local to `implement.py`; prefer
  reuse of `herdr_pane.py`'s resolution/fail-open conventions either way.

  completion (fresh session per child) — the headless drive this item extends.
- **SA-0MUWBHEEF002A6BO** — When running implement on a parent item implement

- **SA-0MTLCCIPU0050Q52** — When implementing an epic start a new session for
  each child — session isolation rule that must be preserved.
- **SA-0MVDQF3VW002PKCA** — User-visible progress feedback during long-running

- **SA-0MTFLQEQQ0083EW1** — Update pane title with status emoticon on skill
  completion — reuse `herdr_pane.update_pane_title` for retained panes.
